title: Ingest incident taxonomy metadata + compute MTTR breakdowns by category/owner
author: Logan Wright
description: Motivation: We’re rolling out incident taxonomy + ownership mapping and need the SLO toolkit to (a) ingest standardized incident metadata and (b) compute MTTR/TTM slices by category and owning team for dashboards + monthly review. Prior to this, incidents were only stored as freeform text and severity, which prevented reliable trend reporting. Summary of changes: Adds a first-class IncidentMetadata schema (category, impacted_surface, owning_team, customer_tier, region, contributing_factors, declared_at/mitigated_at/resolved_at) and wires ingestion from the incident event stream into the SLO toolkit datastore. Adds MTTR aggregations by (severity, category, owning_team) with optional breakdowns by region/tier. Design notes: Category/impacted_surface/contributing_factors are stored as normalized enums but ingestion is tolerant of unknown values (stored as "unknown" + raw_value for analysis); owning_team is sourced from the incident record if present, otherwise derived via existing service->team mapping (with an explicit "owner_source" field for auditing). MTTR is computed as resolved_at - declared_at; mitigation time is mitigated_at - declared_at when available; partial incidents (missing timestamps) are excluded from MTTR aggregates and counted in a "missing_fields" metric. Migration/compat: Backfills are supported by a one-time reindex job (no required runtime migration for existing consumers); existing MTTR queries remain valid (they default to "all" category/owner). Public API: Adds /v1/metrics/incident/mttr?group_by=category,owner_team&from=...&to=... (internal) plus corresponding library method IncidentAnalytics.mttr_breakdown(). Testing: Unit tests for enum mapping + unknown values, MTTR computation edge cases (reopened incidents, missing mitigated_at), and ingestion end-to-end with a fixture payload matching incident-bot vNext fields. Rollout: Land behind INCIDENT_METADATA_V1 feature flag; enable in staging immediately; production enable after incident-bot PR 218 deploy + first 24h validation in dashboards. Related: ENG-4827 (dashboards), ENG-4822 (taxonomy fields), ENG-4825 (allowed values enforcement).
